items.title: 'We fell behind' - what does new San Siro deal mean for AC Milan and Inter?
items.summary: Generali Stadium will have 71,500-seat capacity Inter fans protest the plans outside gala event Inter and Milan have unveiled plans for their new Generali Stadium, which will replace the shared San Siro venue from the 2031-32 season. The stadium, sponsored by Generali – Italy’s largest insurance company – will have a capacity of 71,500 seats and is expected to cost the two clubs €1.2bn (£1bn). The plans were revealed at a gala event at Milan’s Castello Sforzesco on Thursday – but some fans in attendance voiced their opposition to San Siro being demolished.
